en.title: Pod Counts After Scale-Ups and Point Resets
en.description:
A log [1,p,x] directly sets the count of 1-based service p to x, which may decrease it; [2,−1,x] raises every count below x to x. Apply the logs in order and return the final array.

The input/output protocol and the explicitly marked supplementary constraints were compiled by this site; upstream solutions are not executed.
en.input: The first line contains n m, the second line contains the initial counts, followed by m lines of logs. 1≤n,m≤200000, initial values are 1..10⁹, assigned values are 0..10⁹, and 1≤p≤n.
en.output: First output n, then output the final n counts.
en.explanation:
The answers to the three public examples are, in order: 4
10 30 10 10; 5
8 8 20 8 10; 1
0. The examples were rechecked by independent enumeration, state search, or direct simulation.
hints: Process the logs in reverse order, maintaining the maximum global raise seen so far. When you reach the last point assignment of a service, its final value is determined; every other service combines its initial value with all the raises.
